_comment: Generated by scripts/conformance_scoreboard.py — per-policy conformance drill-down for one jurisdiction. Do not hand-edit.

policies.note: rates-given-category — PE-UK applies the AA rate table over a frozen aa_category FRS input. In-scope uncovered — the rate params are compared in the matrix but no AA program surface runs in either PE suite yet (matrix row 14 → SSCBA 1992 s.64-67).
In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes business_rates but rulespec has not encoded it and no suite runs (matrix row 7 → LGFA 1988 Pt III multiplier + reliefs).
In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes capital_gains_tax but rulespec has not encoded it and no suite runs (matrix row 9 → TCGA 1992; FA rate schedule).

rates-given-category — the carer-support-payment-final suite compares the rules-computed entitlement amount (carer_support_payment_annual_amount); PE-UK's carer_support_payment (the Scotland CA replacement, ≥2025) is a hybrid amount-or-reported variable, so the bound comparison is the rate/amount given the award, not the full eligibility rule (matrix row 28).

rates-given-category — the carers-allowance-final suite compares the rules-computed entitlement amount (carers_allowance_annual_amount); PE-UK's carers_allowance variable is a hybrid (care-hours test OR reported fallback, zeroed in Scotland ≥2025), so the bound comparison is the rate/amount given the award, not the full hours-eligibility rule (matrix row 19).

PE-UK carries council_tax as a reported FRS liability (no formula): it applies no bands/valuation and computes no statutory charge, so there is no simulated surface to compare. In-scope uncovered on the rulespec side once PE adds a computed base (matrix row 6 → LGFA 1992 Pt I).

Legacy pre-2013 Council Tax Benefit: PE-UK reads a *_reported amount and applies only a passthrough, never computing the abolished scheme's award from statute. The current-scheme analogue is council_tax_reduction (a distinct in-scope program). Not a comparable statutory surface (matrix row 20).

Covered by the uk-council-tax-reduction case-grid suite. council_tax_reduction gained a formula in PE-UK 2.89.2 (#1769 national core + #1771 Kingston, both merged), resolving the matrix ambiguity at HEAD 45eb181c where the variable was absent. The suite compares PE-UK's England pension-age path (gov.local_authorities.england.council_tax_reduction.pensioners: max-support 1, capital limit 16000, withdrawal 0.20) against the rulespec SI 2012/2885 England pension-age scheme (uk/policies/govuk/council-tax-reduction.yaml) on a synthetic pensioner grid, bridging PE's own applicable amount / applicable income / non-dependant deductions / council_tax liability / savings into the rulespec supplied inputs (the uk-pension-credit bridge pattern). council_tax is a supplied input on both sides, so the schemes are commensurable; all 11 cases match to the penny (the taper interior, the capital screen, single and couple), residuals sub-0.001 (PE float32), inside tolerance. The England pension-age income test does not inherit the #1794 Housing Benefit earnings-disregard defect — council_tax_reduction_applicable_income applies no earnings disregard. matrix row 29 → LGFA 1992 s.13A + Sch.1A; SI 2012/2885.

rates-given-category — PE-UK applies the DLA care/mobility rate tables over a frozen dla_sc_category/dla_m_category FRS input, so the comparison binds the rate schedule, not the award-eligibility rules. Compared via disability-living-allowance-final (matrix row 16).

Contributory ESA is a pure reported passthrough in PE-UK (no formula) — the value carries the FRS-reported award, computing no WRAG/support components. Nothing statutory to compare (matrix row 17 → WRA 2007 Pt 1).

Income-related ESA: PE-UK reads esa_income_reported and applies only a capital/tariff screen, never computing WRAG/support components or the means-test award from statute. The tariff-income helper alone is compared in uk-tax-benefits-efrs, but the program-level award is a reported ceiling — no statutory maximum to bind (matrix row 23 → ESA Regs 2008).
In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes fuel_duty but rulespec has not encoded it and no suite runs (matrix row 10 → HODA 1979 rates).

Incapacity Benefit, Armed Forces Compensation Scheme (afcs) and Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit (iidb) are pure reported passthroughs in PE-UK (no formulas) — legacy/closed benefits carried from microdata, computing no entitlement. Nothing statutory to compare (matrix row 25).
In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes the Scottish LBTT and Welsh LTT transaction taxes but rulespec has not encoded them and no suite runs (matrix row 31 → LTT(S)A 2013 / LTTA(W) 2017).

In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes income_support and applies a tariff screen to jsa_income; WTC/CTC are reported inputs. All £0 in 2026 under UC migration; only tariff/rate helpers are compared, no final award surface runs (matrix row 30).

rates-given-category — PE-UK applies the PIP daily-living/mobility rate tables over a frozen pip_dl_category/pip_m_category FRS input, so the comparison binds the rate schedule, not the award-eligibility rules. Compared via personal-independence-payment-final (matrix row 8).

Severe Disablement Allowance (closed legacy benefit): PE-UK reads sda_reported and multiplies by a max rate, computing no eligibility from statute. Only the rate parameter is compared in the matrix; the program award is a reported ceiling (matrix row 32 → SSCBA 1992 s.68).

Sure Start Maternity Grant: PE-UK reads ssmg_reported and multiplies by the £500 rate, computing no eligibility from statute. Only the rate parameter is compared in the matrix; the program award is a reported ceiling (matrix row 33 → uksi/2005/3061).

PE-UK takes stamp_duty_land_tax straight from microdata (no formula) — the SDLT tier liability is a reported input, not a computed surface. The residential/non-residential SDLT transaction sub-variables (sdlt_on_*_property_transactions) exist and compute, but no program output binds them to a comparison (matrix row 13 → FA 2003 Pt 4).

In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes state_pension (basic+new+additional) from accrual rules, but no final suite runs; the state-pension bridge surface was removed when rulespec re-grounded to accrual basis (matrix row 4 → Pensions Act 2014).

In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes tax_free_childcare but only the top-up rate/ceiling params are compared; no final payment surface runs, and PE frames the rate as 20% vs statute 25% (matrix row 27 → Childcare Payments Act 2014).
In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes tv_licence and free_tv_licence_value but only the fee parameter is compared; no over-75/concession final surface runs (matrix row 34 → uksi/2004/692).
In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes vat (output/input/net) but no PE VAT oracle surface runs; rulespec has a rate-only shell. The largest indirect-tax gap (matrix row 1 → VATA 1994 Sch.7A-9).

In-scope uncovered — PE-UK computes winter_fuel_allowance (2024 PC-only restriction, zeroed in Scotland) but only rate params are compared; no final WFA program surface runs (matrix row 24 → uksi/2025/969; Scotland PAWHP separate).
